name: Resolan
description: Resolan is a broad emotional stabilizer designed to counteract the peaks and crashes generated by heavy pharmaceutical emotional regulation — a 'reset' drug that returns the user's affective baseline to a neutral, functional midpoint after extreme emotional pharmaceutical experiences. It is the pharmacological equivalent of a system reboot: it does not produce any particular feeling, but terminates the residual states left by other drugs and returns the user to an approximation of their natural emotional baseline. It is commonly taken after Drivacor crashes, Lethex grief floods, Syndrel bond dissolution, and Arravex comedowns.
effects: termination of lingering pharmaceutical emotional states
return to approximate natural affective baseline
reduced emotional volatility in post-drug windows
sense of groundedness and present-moment self-awareness
side_effects: if natural baseline is itself significantly dysregulated, Resolan returns users to that baseline — which may be depression, anxiety, or chronic pain
some users find the neutrality of Resolan preferable to baseline and begin using it as a primary drug rather than a reset — a concerning use pattern
blunts the tail-end of positive emotional pharmaceutical effects as well as negative ones
in heavy poly-drug users, Resolan interactions are unpredictable — some combinations produce brief but intense emotional surges before reset
cultural_context: Resolan is the drug that proves how normalized pharmaceutical emotional cycling has become in GLMZ. Its existence as a mainstream product — a drug to fix what other drugs did to you — is taken as completely unremarkable. Tier 3 professionals keep it in their desk drawers. It's sold over the counter in corporate pharmacies alongside protein bars and BCI charge cables. On the Gray Zone, it's used to manage the rougher comedowns from unlicensed drug variants, and is one of the few pharmaceuticals that harm-reduction networks distribute freely without prescription. There is a small but vocal community of people who live exclusively in the Resolan neutral state — taking it to interrupt every emotional experience. Psychiatrists have named the condition 'affective avoidance syndrome.' The people who have it say they prefer it.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 man has been taking Resolan three times a day for a year, interrupting every emotional experience before it fully registers. He functions perfectly. He feels nothing has happened to him for twelve months. His wife says she's been trying to leave him for six months but he keeps resetting before it lands.

A the Gray Zone harm-reduction worker distributing Resolan discovers that the latest batch from Novafold contains an unlisted compound — something that isn't in the public formula. She needs to know what it is and why it's there.

A Helix researcher has developed a version of Resolan that can selectively reset a specific emotional event rather than blanket-resetting to baseline — targeted emotional erasure. Lazarus wants to acquire the patent. Several intelligence agencies want the compound. The researcher wants to destroy it.
